Consult Summary:
- Acute left-sided headache with photophobia and morning onset in a patient with a history of anxiety; plan includes analgesia, stress reduction, sleep and hydration measures, and a follow-up in one week.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Woke this morning with a very severe left-sided headache, described as headachey and prominent on the left side.
- Onset and progression: Symptoms started this morning around 05:30; currently present.
- Symptoms and features: Light sensitivity (photophobia) with mild eye soreness; no neck stiffness; no fever; initial dizziness that resolved; headache worsened with onset of discomfort when lying down but improves after getting comfortable; pain not relieved by paracetamol taken earlier this morning.
- Exposures and triggers: Stress at work for the past couple of months with late nights; history of anxiety.
- Past medical history: Anxiety disorder diagnosed ~2 years ago; on Sertraline; no prior high blood pressure; no other illnesses noted.
- Medications: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); Paracetamol taken this morning (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Patient reports no known drug allergies.
- Family history: No migraines reported in family; mother has anxiety.
- Social history: Lives with partner; non-smoker; has a cat; exercises ~3 times per week (running); diet is adequate but not strictly healthy; work-related stress ongoing.
- Systems review: Headache with photophobia; no neck stiffness; no fever; no persistent nausea; dizziness earlier in the day but resolved; no vomiting reported; no other systemic symptoms described.

Past Medical History:
- Anxiety disorder (diagnosed ~2 years ago); on Sertraline.
- No hypertension or known major medical illnesses documented.
- No known drug allergies.

- Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Paracetamol (taken this morning; dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:

- Diet: Acceptable; not strictly healthy.

- Vitals: Not documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or resulted at this visit.
- Plan noted to consider blood tests or other investigations only if symptoms fail to improve.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute headache with differential for tension-type headache vs migraine
  - Plan:
    - Ibuprofen as first-line analgesic for migraine-type headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Continue Paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Advise possible work-related stress contribution; consider reducing stress.
    - Encourage adequate sleep: minimum 7–8 hours per night.
    - Hydration: 1.5–2 liters of fluids per day (excluding coffee/tea).
    - Consider counselling options; provide link for self-referral.
    - Recommend taking time off work for one week with self-certification.
    - Follow-up in one week to reassess; if not improving, potential blood tests or further evaluation discussed.
    - Safety: Provided information about danger signs of headaches in notes; advised to contact if symptoms worsen or new alarming symptoms occur.

- Issue 2: Anxiety/stress management (in context of current headache)
  - Plan:
    - Continue Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Explore reduction of work-related stress; pursue counselling services as above.

General Plan:
- Follow-up appointment in one week with GP or another clinician to reassess symptoms.
- If symptoms worsen or new red-flag symptoms develop, contact medical advice sooner.
